decks.module: Lane sharing and school bus stops
decks.domain: New laws, office conduct and test-day checklists

cards.front: What does Minnesota law now allow a motorcycle to do between lanes, and what is your duty?
cards.back: In Minnesota a motorcycle may legally ride or pass in the space between your vehicle and a vehicle in the next lane, and you must not get in the way of its safe movement.
cards.memory_hook: Riders may split; you make room

cards.front: Where will you most often see motorcycles sharing lanes, and where else may they pass?
cards.back: You will most often see motorcycle lane sharing at a stoplight as riders move up to the front, but riders may also pass slow traffic on your left or right while using part of your lane.
cards.memory_hook: Stoplight front, or past slow traffic

cards.front: Is a motorcycle riding between lanes breaking the law?
cards.back: A motorcycle sharing your lane or riding between lanes is acting legally, so the driver's duty is to leave it room rather than block it.

cards.front: What do flashing red lights on a school bus tell drivers?
cards.back: Flashing red lights on a school bus tell drivers that students are boarding or leaving the bus.

cards.front: How close may you stop to a school bus whose red lights are flashing?
cards.back: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop your vehicle no closer than twenty feet from the bus.

cards.front: Must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if its stop arm is folded?
cards.back: You must stop for a school bus showing flashing red lights even when its stop arm has not swung out.

cards.front: What is the one exception to stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights?
cards.back: The one exception to stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights is when you are on a divided highway and traveling in the opposite direction.

cards.front: What can happen if you fail to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
cards.back: Failing to stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing can bring fines and a suspension of your driver's license.

cards.front: How far must you stop from a school bus with flashing red lights, and what is the sole exception?
cards.back: Upon seeing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop at least twenty feet away unless you are traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway.
cards.memory_hook: Twenty feet back unless divided opposite

cards.front: What triggers your duty to stop for a school bus: the stop arm or the red lights?
cards.back: The trigger for stopping at a school bus is the flashing red lights, not the stop arm, so a bus whose arm stays folded still requires you to stop at least twenty feet away.

decks.module: Work zones, DVS offices and online tools
decks.domain: New laws, office conduct and test-day checklists

cards.front: What should you watch for in a work zone, and why?
cards.back: In a work zone, stay alert for distracted driving, zipper merges and changed lane patterns, because crews work very close to moving traffic and large construction vehicles can move unpredictably.

cards.front: Which three hazards does the work zone reminder name together?
cards.back: The work-zone reminder names three hazards to watch for together: distracted driving, zipper merges and lanes that have been shifted or altered.

cards.front: Is interfering with the work of a DVS employee a crime in Minnesota?
cards.back: Interfering with or obstructing the work of a Driver and Vehicle Services employee is a crime under Minnesota Statute six hundred nine point five zero, Subdivision five.

cards.front: What happens to a customer who is abusive, disruptive or violent at a DVS office?
cards.back: Driver and Vehicle Services does not tolerate disruptive behavior or harassment, obscene or abusive language or gestures, interfering with services, refusing staff instructions, or violent conduct; a customer who does any of these is asked to leave and police are called.

cards.front: Are interfering with and obstructing a DVS employee covered by the same statute?
cards.back: Interfering with a DVS employee and obstructing a DVS employee are both described as crimes under the same statute, Minnesota Statute six hundred nine point five zero, Subdivision five.

cards.front: What reminder does the Commissioner's message give about the driving privilege?
cards.back: The Commissioner's message reminds drivers that driving is a privilege that carries a responsibility to everyone else on the road: buckle up, obey speed laws and never drive under the influence of alcohol.

cards.front: How does the DVS online pre-application save time at the office?
cards.back: The pre-application in DVS online services lets you finish a large part of your license application before the visit and lists the documents each license type requires, which shortens your time at the counter.

cards.front: When should you begin the online pre-application before an office visit, and what do you bring?
cards.back: Begin the online pre-application no more than thirty days before your office visit so you do not have to fill out a paper application, and bring the confirmation page together with every document it lists.

cards.front: What online help does DVS offer for questions and tracking your records?
cards.back: Driver and Vehicle Services offers a virtual assistant at drive.mn.gov in English, Spanish, Somali and Hmong, and a MyDVS account lets you follow your license and registration information online.

cards.front: Is the thirty-day pre-application window the same as a permit holding period?
cards.back: The thirty-day window governs when you start the online pre-application before an office visit, and the manual ties staying inside it to avoiding a paper application; it is not a permit holding period.

decks.domain: New laws, office conduct and test-day checklists

cards.front: Before the written test, what appointment and online step does the checklist require?
cards.back: Before the Class D written test you need a scheduled test appointment, and the checklist says to finish the online pre-application at dps.mn.gov slash mydvs within the thirty days before that appointment, not earlier.

cards.front: Besides an appointment, what must you bring or know for the written test?
cards.back: For the written test, bring the required identification and money for the fees, and know your Social Security number if you are eligible to have one.

cards.front: How old must an applicant under eighteen be to take the written test?
cards.back: An applicant younger than eighteen must be at least fifteen years old to take the written test.

cards.front: Which two cards can a teen bring to show driver education status for the written test?
cards.back: An applicant under eighteen brings either a Blue Card, showing classroom instruction is finished and behind-the-wheel training is scheduled, or a Pink Card, showing enrollment in a concurrent driver education course with the first fifteen classroom hours completed.

cards.front: Who may sign and approve the application of a written test applicant under eighteen?
cards.back: Written test applicants under eighteen must be at least fifteen, bring a Blue Card or Pink Card, bring the Supplemental Parental Curriculum completion certificate if completed, and have an approved adult sign the application with documentation when not a parent.

cards.front: How does the Blue Card differ from the Pink Card?
cards.back: The Blue Card shows classroom instruction is complete and behind-the-wheel training is arranged, while the Pink Card shows enrollment in a concurrent course with the first fifteen classroom hours done; either one admits a teen to the written test.

cards.front: Is the minimum teen age for the written test the same as for the road test?
cards.back: A teen must be at least fifteen years old for the written test, a different age from the road test minimum on the next checklist page.

decks.module: Road test day: driver, permit and vehicle
decks.domain: New laws, office conduct and test-day checklists

cards.front: What do you need for the road test besides your appointment and pre-application?
cards.back: For the road test you need an appointment, a completed online pre-application, and a licensed driver who comes with you; without that licensed driver the road test may be cancelled.

cards.front: What do you hand the examiner at the road test?
cards.back: At the road test you hand your valid instruction permit to the examiner.

cards.front: What must be true of the vehicle you bring to the road test?
cards.back: The road test vehicle must be safe: doors open from inside and outside, seat belts work, and the headlights, taillights, brake lights and turn signals all function, with registration that is current or covered by a sixty-day permit.

cards.front: Which forms of proof of insurance are accepted for the road test vehicle?
cards.back: Proof of insurance for the road test vehicle can be the original card from the insurance company, the policy declaration page, or electronic proof from the insurer's website or shown on a device.

cards.front: Is electronic proof of insurance accepted at the road test?
cards.back: Electronic proof of insurance from the insurer's website or on a device is accepted for the road test, alongside the original card or the policy declaration page.

decks.domain: New laws, office conduct and test-day checklists

cards.front: How old must a teen be for the road test, and which card must they bring?
cards.back: A road test applicant under eighteen must be at least sixteen years old and bring the White Card showing driver education was completed.

cards.front: How long must a teen have held a permit before the road test, and with what record?
cards.back: A road test applicant under eighteen must have held an instruction permit for the past six months with no conviction for a moving violation or for an alcohol or controlled substance violation.

cards.front: What does a teen bring if some permit driving happened in another state?
cards.back: If some or all of a teen's six months of permit driving took place in another state, the teen brings a certified driving record from that state to show eligibility for the provisional license.

cards.front: Which signed driving record and approval does a teen bring to the road test?
cards.back: A road test applicant under eighteen brings a Supervised Driving Log that is filled in and signed by a parent or guardian, plus the parental approval signature on the application.

cards.front: How long must eighteen-year-olds and applicants nineteen or older hold a permit before the road test?
cards.back: An eighteen-year-old road test applicant must have held the instruction permit for at least six months, while an applicant aged nineteen or older needs at least three months.

cards.front: Which card does a teen bring to the road test instead of the Blue or Pink Card?
cards.back: A teen must be at least sixteen years old for the road test and brings the White Card, which certifies completed driver education, rather than the Blue or Pink enrollment card.

cards.front: Which applicants need six months of permit holding, and which need only three?
cards.back: Permit holding time before the road test is six months for applicants under eighteen and for eighteen-year-olds, but only three months for applicants aged nineteen or older.

cards.front: What extra condition applies to a teen's six months of permit holding?
cards.back: For teens the six months of permit holding must also be free of convictions for moving violations and alcohol or controlled substance violations, a condition the adult checklist lines do not repeat.

recaps.module: Lane sharing and school bus stops

recap_hooks.text: Motorcycles may legally share or split lanes, so give them room rather than blocking them.
Flashing red school bus lights mean stop at least twenty feet back, stop arm or not, unless you are going the other way on a divided highway.
Skipping a school bus stop can bring fines and a suspended license.

recaps.module: Work zones, DVS offices and online tools

recap_hooks.text: Work zones demand attention to distracted drivers, zipper merges and shifted lanes.
DVS staff are protected by law, and disruptive or abusive customers are asked to leave while police are called.
Start the online pre-application within thirty days of your visit and bring the confirmation page and listed documents.
The written test needs an appointment, a pre-application, identification, fee money and your Social Security number if you have one.
Teens must be at least fifteen and bring a Blue or Pink Card plus an approved application.

recaps.module: Road test day: driver, permit and vehicle

recap_hooks.text: Road test day means an appointment, a pre-application, a licensed driver and your permit for the examiner.
The vehicle must be safe, registered and insured, and electronic insurance proof is fine.
Teens take the road test at sixteen or older with the White Card, a signed log and six violation-free months of permit holding.
Eighteen-year-olds also need six months of permit holding, but applicants nineteen or older need three.
